case_name: Krishnakumari Thampuran vs Palace Administration Board

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Krishnakumari Thampuran, member of Cochin Royal Family

facts_of_case: Member of Cochin Royal Family fighting for rights in family property; properties exempted from Hindu Succession Act; embargo on right to institute suit for partition.

legal_principles.principle: A child born before a decree of nullity is granted shall be deemed to be the legitimate child of the parties to the marriage.
legal_principles.held: decree it had been dissolved instead of being annulled, shall be deemed to be their legitimate child notwithstanding the decree of nullity.

legal_principles.principle: Illegitimate children are entitled to claim shares in the coparcenery property along with legitimate children.
legal_principles.held: the proposition that illegitimate children are, by their own right, entitled to claim shares in the coparcenery property along with legitimate children is a logical extension to the principle laid down

legal_principles.principle: Illegitimate children have proprietary rights for succession, but confined to the right in properties of their parents.
legal_principles.held: although illegitimate children do have proprietary rights for succession, the same is confined to right in properties of their parents and not to any other properties.

use_for_drafting: drafting partition cases involving royal families
advising on Hindu succession and marriage laws
assisting in disputes over joint family properties
